newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Izetbegovic agrees to sack Minister - U.S..
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic agrees to sack Minister - U.S..

text.p: Bosnia's president bowed to U.S. pressure on Friday and agreed to fire two senior defense officials, including one with strong ties to Iran, clearing the way for delivery of a massive shipment of American arms, a U.S. envoy said.

"President (Alija) Izetbegovic informed us and gave us the documents which would remove Deputy Minister Hasan Cengic and Minister Vladimir Soljic from office," U.S. special envoy James Pardew told Reuters in Sarajevo on Friday.
"The documents must be signed by (Moslem-Croat) federation President Kresimir Zubak before they go into effect. We have asked for an immediate meeting with Zubak to complete the process."

But Izetbegovic, a Moslem, said in a television interview later on Friday evening that Zubak, a Croat, was refusing to sign the necessary papers and trying to link the action to other, unrelated government issues.
"At this moment Zubak is refusing to sign," Izetbegovic said on government television.
"We do care about the 'train and equip programme' but it might be that the Croats care less... It might be that they have some other way to get arms, which I don't doubt."
The Dayton peace accord which ended fighting in Bosnia last year divides the country between the Moslem-Croat federation and a Serb republic. Each national group has retained its own army.
The United States is sponsoring a $400 million "train and equip" programme intended to bring the Moslem-Croat federation's forces up to parity with the Bosnian Serbs.
But the start of the programme was held up for weeks this summer with Moslems and Croats squabbled.
A cargo vessel with $100 million dollars worth of military equipment bound for Bosnia has been idling in the Adriatic, waiting for Sarajevo to remove Cengic, since October 24.

Pardew said the American Condor, bearing tanks, helicopters, automatic rifles, machine-guns and ammunition, could dock in the Croatian port of Ploce within hours of Zubak's signature and begin off-loading within days.
In order to bill the dismissal as a reorganization within the Bosnian-Croat federation, the government has insisted that Soljic, a Croat, must go at the same time as Cengic, a Moslem.
Pardew said Izetbegovic has nominated Ante Jelavic, a Croat, as the new Defense Minister, and Sakib Mahmuljin, a Moslem as the deputy to replace Cengic.

The American military contractor hired to oversee U.S. arms deliveries to the Bosnian army despatched a team to the Croatian port of Ploce on Friday to prepare for possible off-loading of the American Condor's cargo.

"We have a group of people in Ploce today checking out the port facilities to be certain everything is ready if the cargo is released," Joseph Allred, spokesman for the contractor, Military Professional Resources Inc. (MPRI), told Reuters.
Iran supplied weapons and ammunition to Sarajevo during the 43-month Bosnian war in violation of the U.N. arms embargo. The United States knew of the deliveries but did not object.
After Dayton, Washington made its arms supplies contingent upon departure of foreign Islamic fighters, known as mujahedin. Most are reported to have left.
